In an interview on Friday, Haugen told CNBC’s “Squawk Box” the companies must “step up and comply.” Haugen said tech companies often follow only the exact written text when dealing with “very flexible systems.”

During her appearance, Haugen also questioned whether AI firms will hold to the “spirit of the rules.” She said they could instead “go around the end of the fence” by exploiting what is not expressly prohibited.

The White House Accord on Super Intelligence, unveiled Tuesday, is not legally binding but calls for stronger internal controls, independent audits and board-level oversight.

Haugen, a former product manager on Facebook’s civic misinformation team, leaked several internal documents to The Wall Street Journal in 2021. The documents became the basis for a series of reports called “The Facebook Files.”
Some of the documents showed the company was aware that its platforms negatively affected teens’ mental health.

Haugen’s story is the focus of “The Social Reckoning,” a new Aaron Sorkin film releasing Oct. 9. She also wrote a book about her role in bringing the documents to light, “The Power of One: How I Found the Strength to Tell the Truth and Why I Blew the Whistle on Facebook.”
